sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed observational law \(P\) on the known face \(\Delta(S)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query fixes \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\); treatment assignment is not randomized by the sampling design.
sampling_model.overlap: Every supported cell is bounded below by \(\epsilon\); forbidden cells remain structural zeros.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only multinomial cell probabilities are estimated by \(\widehat P_N\); the graph, exact support, and successful rational certificate are treated as supplied.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.1 identifies or zeros a district \(Q\)-factor under specified positive-prefix conditions.
Theorem 2 maps quasi-Markovian observational constraints to exact separate credal sets for the latent roots.
Theorem 4 represents compatible quasi-Markovian functional SCMs exactly by a credal network.
Theorem 1 returns sharp extrema of a discrete causal query through a canonical polynomial program.
Theorem 1 shows the arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut method is at least as complete as classical identification under strict positivity.
Proposition 8 shows variable-state cardinality constraints alone do not improve semi-Markovian identification.
Theorems 2--3 make do-search sound and complete in domains already completely characterized by do-calculus.
Theorem 8 derives the efficient influence function for a graph-derived functional under primal fixability.

body.tldr: Exact structural zeros are treated as identifying information rather than as failed overlap. In a finite acyclic canonical SCM with one independent response root per bidirected-clique district, first-forbidden-prefix saturation produces the unique maximal Cartesian response support compatible with the supplied realizable observational support. Positive-prefix telescoping recovers linear district signatures. A deterministic intervention query is uniformly identified on the support face exactly when its response indicator lies in the tensor product of those signature row spaces. Membership yields one denominator-safe rational functional; nonmembership yields strictly positive rational same-support, same-law SCM twins with distinct causal answers. The rational output has direct multinomial influence-function inference on fixed interiors, while a sound-and-complete support-scoped do-search normalization remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing work either checks positivity for a formula, certifies selected constrained instances, or numerically optimizes over compatible response laws. It does not give a necessary-and-sufficient support-only criterion uniform over every same-law model on a realizable exact support face.
project_justification.niche: Independent district roots turn observational zeros into a maximal product support and turn supported prefix ratios into separately identified linear signatures. This creates a finite tensor geometry not exposed by full-support do-calculus or generic polynomial optimization.
project_justification.fill: The project proves support saturation, signature recovery, the tensor iff theorem, a rational formula-or-rational-twins dichotomy, and fixed-face multinomial inference, then asks whether signed product-preserving search rules can compile the semantic criterion without enumerating the full tensor.

body.related_work: Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee supply the writing model: strict positivity fails, positive prefixes can still license \(Q\)-factor operations, and a complete data-adaptive identifier remains unresolved. Zaffalon, Antonucci, and Cabañas, together with their 2024 journal extension, supply the closest method model: quasi-Markovian observations induce separate linear credal constraints and counterfactual bounds follow by credal inference. Their rootwise linearization is treated as established groundwork, while maximal support and the face-uniform symbolic formula-or-twins criterion are the proposed delta. Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser justify canonical finite response types and exact polynomial optimization; Shridharan and Iyengar show how district factorization reduces multilinear degree. Chen and Darwiche show that constrained identifiability can exploit circuit invariants and also clarify that mere state-cardinality restrictions do not create the joint-support information used here. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen provide the search-state and rule-soundness exemplar for the open compiler question. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser provide the differentiation template for converting an identified graphical functional into influence-function inference.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The semantic tensor criterion permits signed rational coefficients and may require contractions that are not expressible in the current prose grammar of support-scoped probability rules. The core therefore does not claim a complete symbolic compiler. It also treats the exact support mask as known; sampling-zero discrimination and local asymptotics across a changing support remain separate problems.
body.honest_scope: The support saturation, district-signature recovery, rational success certificate, rational interior failure certificate, tensor iff characterization, destructive controls, and fixed-face multinomial inference are theorem claims to be proved. The do-search normalization is explicitly open. The model class has one mutually independent finite root for each bidirected-clique district and does not include overlapping independent latent-parent neighborhoods. Under full support, the criterion must accept every classically identified query and its functional must agree with the classical answer; the diagonal bow and five-cell instrumental-variable controls test the structural-zero boundary. Support recovery, optimized bit complexity, and empirical software integration are outside scope.
